target: Nós somos de Belo Horizonte.
english: We're from Belo Horizonte.
tip: 'Ser' + 'de' for origin: 'nós somos de Belo Horizonte.' This is permanent identity, so use 'ser.'

target: Ele tem medo de avião.
english: He's afraid of flying.
tip: 'Ter medo de' means 'to be afraid of' – literally 'to have fear of.' Many English 'be' expressions use 'ter' in Portuguese.

target: Nós estamos planejando uma viagem.
english: We're planning a trip.
tip: `estar + gerúndio` = English '-ing right now': `estou comendo` = 'I'm eating'. Brazilians use this way more than Spanish/Italian use their gerundios.

target: O trânsito está horrível hoje.
english: Traffic is terrible today.
tip: Traffic conditions change daily – use 'estar.' If you said 'o trânsito é horrível,' you'd mean it's always terrible.

target: Nós estamos cansados depois do trabalho.
english: We're tired after work.
tip: 'Estar' is for temporary states. Being tired is something that changes – you won't be tired forever.

target: Eu tenho saudade da minha cidade.
english: I miss my city.
tip: `-inho` softens tone: `um momentinho` (just a sec), `obrigadinho` (thanks, friendly). Not about size – about warmth.

target: Qual é o seu número de telefone?
english: What's your phone number?
tip: 'Qual é' = what is (choosing/identifying). 'Número de telefone' = phone number.

target: Qual restaurante você recomenda?
english: Which restaurant do you recommend?
tip: 'Qual' for recommendations: 'Qual restaurante você recomenda?' asks to pick one from many.

target: Quando fecha o supermercado?
english: When does the supermarket close?
tip: -o usually m (o livro), -a usually f (a casa). Exceptions: o problema (m), o dia (m), a mão (f). The article is the real signal.

target: Vocês estão gostando da cidade?
english: Are you enjoying the city?
tip: Endings: -ar → -ando, -er → -endo, -ir → -indo. `Comendo`, `bebendo`, `dormindo`. Always paired with `estar`.

target: O quarto está uma bagunça.
english: The room is a mess.
tip: The room can be cleaned – the mess is a temporary state, so use 'estar.' If you said 'é uma bagunça,' you'd mean it's inherently messy.

target: Eu estou fazendo um curso online.
english: I'm taking an online course.
tip: 'Fazer' is irregular: eu faço, você faz. 'Faço' has a soft 'c' (ç sound).

target: A comida brasileira é muito saborosa.
english: Brazilian food is very tasty.
tip: 'Ser' for inherent characteristics of things: 'A comida brasileira é saborosa' – this describes its nature, not a temporary state.

target: O elevador está quebrado de novo.
english: The elevator is broken again.
tip: 'Estar' is used for location of people and movable objects – where something or someone is right now.

target: Por que a loja está fechada?
english: Why is the store closed?
tip: 'Por que' (two words, no accent) = why (in questions). 'Porque' (one word) = because (in answers).

target: Onde tem uma farmácia por perto?
english: Where is there a pharmacy nearby?
tip: `Há` exists in PT but sounds formal/written. `Tem` is what you'll hear in speech. Same word as the verb 'to have' – context tells you which.

target: Ele é muito gentil com todo mundo.
english: He's very kind to everyone.
tip: Personality traits use 'ser' – they're part of who you are. 'É gentil' = he's a kind person (inherently).

target: Ela tem muito talento.
english: She has a lot of talent.
tip: Brazilians use `tem` for 'there is/are' instead of `há`: `tem uma farmácia aqui` = 'there's a pharmacy here'. Same `ter` (to have) doing double duty.

target: Ela está linda nesse vestido.
english: She looks beautiful in that dress.
tip: 'Estar bonita/linda' = she looks beautiful right now. 'Ser bonita/linda' = she IS beautiful (always). Both are compliments but with different nuances.

target: Onde posso carregar o celular?
english: Where can I charge my phone?
tip: 'Onde' = where. 'Aonde' = where to (with motion verbs): 'aonde você vai?'

target: Meu pai é professor de história.
english: My dad is a history teacher.
tip: 'Ser' for someone's profession or occupation: 'Meu pai é professor.' Professions are seen as defining characteristics.

target: Nós vamos ao cinema hoje à noite.
english: We're going to the movies tonight.
tip: 'Ir' is highly irregular: eu vou, nós vamos, vocês vão. 'Ir a' = to go to (with article: 'ao cinema').

target: A festa é na casa do Pedro.
english: The party is at Pedro's house.
tip: Event locations use 'ser': 'a festa é na casa' = the party takes place at the house. This is about where the event happens, not where something is located.

target: A gente vai ver o pôr do sol.
english: We're going to watch the sunset.
tip: 'Ver' means to see and is irregular: vejo, vê, vemos, veem. 'Pôr do sol' (sunset) uses the older infinitive 'pôr' (to put/set).

target: A gente vai de carro ou de metrô?
english: Are we going by car or subway?
tip: 'Ir' is one of the most used verbs – besides 'to go', it forms the informal future: 'vou fazer' (I'm going to do).

target: Eu tenho certeza de que vai dar certo.
english: I'm sure it's going to work out.
tip: 'Ter certeza' means 'to be sure' – literally 'to have certainty.' 'Dar certo' means 'to work out' and is one of the most useful Brazilian expressions.

target: Eu sou alto, mas meu irmão é baixo.
english: I'm tall, but my brother is short.
tip: 'Ser' is for permanent physical traits. Height doesn't change, so 'sou alto' uses ser.

target: Como eu chego na rodoviária?
english: How do I get to the bus station?
tip: 'Como eu chego' = how do I get to. 'Rodoviária' = bus station (for intercity buses).

target: Nós temos muito trabalho essa semana.
english: We have a lot of work this week.
tip: The accent on 'têm' (they have) distinguishes it from 'tem' (he/she has) – this distinction only exists in writing.

target: A porta está aberta, pode entrar.
english: The door is open, you can come in.
tip: The door can be opened or closed – it's a changeable state, so use 'estar.'

target: A fruta está madura, pode comer.
english: The fruit is ripe, you can eat it.
tip: The fruit wasn't always ripe – it became ripe. Conditions that result from change use 'estar.'

target: Ele está no aeroporto esperando o voo.
english: He's at the airport waiting for the flight.
tip: Use 'estar' for temporary location of people. He's at the airport now but won't be there forever.

target: Vocês vão à praia neste fim de semana?
english: Are you going to the beach this weekend?
tip: 'Ir a' means to go to. 'Ir' is completely irregular: vou, vai, vamos, vão. It's also used to form the future: 'vou fazer' = I'm going to do.

target: Ela é advogada, mas está trabalhando como professora.
english: She's a lawyer, but she's working as a teacher.
tip: 'Ser' for profession (permanent identity) vs 'estar' for current activity (temporary). She IS a lawyer but she's currently working as a teacher.

target: Essa escola é uma das melhores da cidade.
english: This school is one of the best in the city.
tip: 'Ser' is used with comparisons and superlatives to describe inherent qualities.

target: Quem ligou para você?
english: Who called you?
tip: 'Quem ligou' = who called. 'Ligar para' = to call (someone). 'Para' is required with 'ligar.'

target: Como posso ajudar?
english: How can I help?
tip: Portuguese questions often have the same word order as statements – just change the intonation.

target: O que tem para comer?
english: What is there to eat?
tip: 'O que tem' is an extremely casual and common way to ask what's available. Literally 'what does it have.'

target: Como se chama esse prato?
english: What's this dish called?
tip: 'Como se chama' literally means 'how does it call itself.' Use it for things and people: 'como se chama esse prato?' or 'como você se chama?'

target: Ela está grávida de seis meses.
english: She's six months pregnant.
tip: Even though pregnancy is temporary, 'estar grávida' is the standard expression – never use 'ser grávida'.

target: Qual ônibus vai para o centro?
english: Which bus goes downtown?
tip: 'Qual' = which/what. Used when choosing from options: 'Qual ônibus?' = Which bus? (among many).

target: Estou preocupado com a situação.
english: I'm worried about the situation.
tip: If the state could change tomorrow → `estar`. Permanent traits → `ser`. `Ele é nervoso` = he's a nervous type (always). `Ele está nervoso` = he's nervous right now.

target: Estou animado para a viagem.
english: I'm looking forward to the trip.
tip: por = reason / exchange / route. para = destination / purpose / recipient. trabalho por dinheiro (for money) vs trabalho para o futuro (for the future).

target: Meu chefe é muito exigente.
english: My boss is very demanding.
tip: Like Spanish, 'ser' is for identity and 'estar' for states – but Portuguese uses 'estar' even more frequently.

target: O preço do aluguel aumentou.
english: The rent price went up.
tip: 'Preço' (price) is masculine: 'o preço.' Words ending in -o are almost always masculine.

target: Ela está cansada depois da viagem.
english: She's tired after the trip.
tip: 'Estar' is for temporary states. She won't be tired forever – it's a condition that will pass.

target: Estou entediado, vamos fazer alguma coisa?
english: I'm bored, let's do something?
tip: Boredom is a temporary emotional state – use 'estar.' 'Ser entediado' would mean you're a boring person, not a bored person!

target: Por que você mudou de emprego?
english: Why did you change jobs?
tip: 'Por que' (why?) is two words. 'Porque' (because) is one word. 'Por quê?' at sentence end.

target: A cozinha do apartamento é pequena.
english: The apartment kitchen is small.
tip: `-inho` softens tone: `um momentinho` (just a sec), `obrigadinho` (thanks, friendly). Not about size – about warmth.

target: Os óculos do meu avô são antigos.
english: My grandfather's glasses are old.
tip: 'Óculos' is always plural and masculine in Portuguese: os óculos. There's no singular form.

target: Quanto custa essa camiseta?
english: How much does this T-shirt cost?
tip: 'Quanto custa' means 'how much does it cost.' You can also say 'quanto é' for a more casual version.

target: Ela é formada em direito.
english: She has a degree in law.
tip: 'Ser formado em' means to have a degree in. Education is a permanent achievement, so it uses 'ser.'

target: As crianças estão nos quartos.
english: The children are in the rooms.
tip: 'Nos' is the contraction of 'em + os' (in the, masculine plural). 'Nas' = 'em + as' (feminine plural).

target: Como é o tempo em Curitiba?
english: What's the weather like in Curitiba?
tip: 'Como é o tempo' = what's the weather like. 'Tempo' means both 'time' and 'weather' in Portuguese.

target: Ela trabalha na recepção do hotel.
english: She works at the hotel reception.
tip: 'Na recepção' = em + a = at/in the. 'Recepção' is feminine – nouns ending in -ção are always feminine.

target: As cortinas da sala são novas.
english: The living room curtains are new.
tip: 'são' – irregular present tense. The most common Portuguese verbs are irregular and must be memorized individually.

target: Onde tem um bom café por aqui?
english: Where can I find a good café around here?
tip: `Há` exists in PT but sounds formal/written. `Tem` is what you'll hear in speech. Same word as the verb 'to have' – context tells you which.

target: A viagem de ônibus demora cinco horas.
english: The bus trip takes five hours.
tip: 'Viagem' is feminine despite ending in -m: a viagem. Other feminine -gem nouns: a garagem, a paisagem, a mensagem.

target: O que tem de bom para fazer aqui?
english: What's there good to do here?
tip: 'O que tem de bom' is a very natural Brazilian way to ask about what's good or available somewhere.

target: A janela do quarto dá para o mar.
english: The bedroom window faces the sea.
tip: 'Dar para' meaning 'to face/overlook' is a very useful expression: 'a janela dá para o mar' = the window faces the sea.
